title: Know thyself
briefing: Every action is checked against WHO you are: your user id and your groups.
tips: `id` shows your uid, gid and groups. `id -u` prints just the numeric user id.
objective: Write your numeric user id (uid) into ~/uid.txt.
hints: There's a command that reports your identity in numbers.
`id` shows everything; `id -u` prints only the uid.
explanation: Your uid is your true name to the kernel — 0 is root, regular users start at 1000. Groups (gid and the extra groups from `id`) decide which 'group' permission bits apply to you.
